\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The phenomenon}
Reduce a monic separable $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $n$ modulo an unramified prime $p$; it factors into distinct irreducibles whose degrees form a partition of $n$, the \emph{splitting type} $\lambda(p)$. Empirically, some splitting questions are answered by congruences and some are not, and the divide is stark rather than gradual.

Two cubics make the point. For $f_1 = x^3 + x^2 - 2x - 1$, the minimal polynomial of $2\cos(2\pi/7)$ generating the real cyclic cubic subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)$, one finds over the first $6541$ primes, with zero exceptions,
\[
  \lambda(p) = [1,1,1] \iff p \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 7,
\]
and no prime ever produces the type $[1,2]$. For $f_2 = x^3+x+1$, of discriminant $-31$, no modulus whatsoever produces such a rule.

This paper explains the dichotomy, proves it in general, computes the exact residual information in the non-pinned cases, determines the maximum information any observable can extract from a binary splitting statistic, and quantifies the collapse of all of this structure when the prime is replaced by a semiprime.

\subsection{The model}
Two classical theorems reduce everything to finite group theory with the uniform measure.

\emph{Chebotarev (1922).} Let $L$ be the splitting field of $f$ and $G = \operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$, viewed inside $S_n$ through its action on the roots. Unramified primes have a well-defined Frobenius conjugacy class, distributed in proportion to class size, and the splitting type of $p$ is the cycle type of the Frobenius. Hence a prime chosen by natural density behaves as a uniformly random $g \in G$.

\emph{Abelian reciprocity (Artin, 1927; classically Kronecker--Weber).} The congruence class of $p$ modulo $m$ determines, and is determined by, the images of the Frobenius under characters of $G$ landing in abelian groups. Every homomorphism $\varphi : G \to A$ with $A$ commutative kills commutators and therefore factors uniquely through $G^{\ab} = G/[G,G]$.

Accordingly we study the uniform probability space $(G,\text{uniform})$; an \emph{observable} is a map $X : G \to \kappa$ into a finite set, and \emph{congruence observables} are those of the form $g \mapsto \varphi(g)$ for a homomorphism $\varphi$ into a finite abelian group.

\subsection{Contributions}
(i) The criterion (\S\ref{sec:crit}): pinning $\iff$ factoring through $G^{\ab}$ $\iff$ commutator invariance, with optimality and conductor detection. (ii) Exact values on $C_3$, $S_3$, $S_4$, $A_5$ (\S\ref{sec:cases}). (iii) The capacity of a binary fork and its rigidity in $S_n$ (\S\ref{sec:cap}). (iv) The extremal profile of an index-two conductor (\S\ref{sec:profile}). (v) The semiprime barrier with a sharp constant and an exact which-factor wall (\S\ref{sec:semi}).

\section{Information-theoretic framework}

All logarithms are natural; values quoted ``in bits'' have been divided by $\log 2$.

\begin{definition}[Empirical law]
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with the uniform measure and $X : \Omega \to \kappa$ with $\kappa$ finite. Then $\PR[X = k] = |X^{-1}(k)|/|\Omega|$, and $\sum_k \PR[X=k] = 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Entropy and mutual information]
With $\eta(t) = -t\log t$ and $\eta(0) = 0$, set
\[
  H(X) = \sum_k \eta(\PR[X=k]), \qquad (X,Y)(\omega) = (X\omega, Y\omega), \qquad
  I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Determination, pinning, flatness, fork]
$X$ \emph{determines} $Y$ if $X\omega = X\omega' \Rightarrow Y\omega = Y\omega'$. The pair is \emph{pinned} if $I(X;Y) = H(Y)$ and \emph{flat} if $I(X;Y) = 0$. A \emph{fork} is an observable with two values; arithmetically, a yes/no function of the splitting type.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Basic properties]\label{thm:basic}
For observables $X : \Omega \to \kappa$, $Y : \Omega \to \beta$ on a finite uniform space:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H(X) \le H(X,Y)$, with equality iff $X$ determines $Y$.
\item \textup{(Pinning identity)} $I(X;Y) = H(Y)$ iff $X$ determines $Y$; otherwise $I(X;Y) < H(Y)$.
\item $I(X;Y) \ge 0$, with equality iff $X$ and $Y$ are independent.
\item $H(X) \le \log|\kappa|$, hence $I(X;Y) \le \min\{H(Y), \log|\kappa|\}$.
\item $I(X;Y) = H(Y) - \mathbb{E}_k[H(Y \mid X = k)]$.
\item \textup{(Data processing)} $I(u \circ X; Y) \le I(X;Y)$ for any $u : \kappa \to \kappa'$.
\item If $X$ determines $X'$ then $I(X';Y) \le I(X;Y)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) $H(X,Y) - H(X) = \sum_k \PR[X=k]H(Y\mid X=k) \ge 0$ by superadditivity $\eta(\sum_i a_i) \le \sum_i \eta(a_i)$ for $a_i \ge 0$, which is strict as soon as two summands in a fibre are positive --- exactly the failure of determination. (2) is (1) rearranged. (3) is Gibbs' inequality applied termwise to $\PR[(X,Y) = (k,b)]$ against $\PR[X=k]\PR[Y=b]$, with the strictness of $\log t < t-1$ giving the equality case. (4) is Jensen. (5) is the computation in (1). (6) is proved by exhibiting the pointwise nonnegative gap
\[
  \Delta(k,b) = r\log\frac{r\,\PR[uX = uk]}{\PR[X=k]\,\PR[(uX,Y)=(uk,b)]}, \qquad r = \PR[(X,Y)=(k,b)],
\]
and showing $\sum_{k,b}\Delta(k,b) = I(X;Y) - I(uX;Y)$. (7) follows from (6) since determination is equivalent to factorization.
\end{proof}

Item (2) is the technical heart: over a finite uniform space, pinning is exactly determination, so an information hypothesis converts into a combinatorial one with no loss.

\section{The fork-pinning criterion}\label{sec:crit}

Let $G$ be finite with the uniform measure, $\pi : G \to G^{\ab}$ the abelianization map.

\begin{theorem}[Structural half]\label{thm:struct}
Let $A$ be finite abelian, $\varphi : G \to A$ a homomorphism, $Y : G \to \beta$. If $\varphi$ determines $Y$, then $\pi$ determines $Y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\varphi = \tilde\varphi \circ \pi$ for the induced $\tilde\varphi$ on $G^{\ab}$; hence $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$ implies $\varphi(x) = \varphi(y)$, and determination transfers.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Fork-pinning criterion]\label{thm:crit}
For $Y : G \to \beta$ the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I(\varphi;Y) = H(Y)$ for some finite abelian $A$ and some homomorphism $\varphi : G \to A$;
\item $Y = \psi \circ \pi$ for some $\psi : G^{\ab} \to \beta$;
\item $Y(gc) = Y(g)$ for all $g \in G$ and all $c \in [G,G]$;
\item $I(\pi;Y) = H(Y)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1)$\Rightarrow$(2): pinning gives determination by Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(2); Theorem~\ref{thm:struct} upgrades it to determination by $\pi$, which is equivalent to factorization through $\pi$. (2)$\Rightarrow$(3): $\pi(gc) = \pi(g)$. (3)$\Rightarrow$(4): commutator invariance says $Y$ is constant on the fibres of $\pi$. (4)$\Rightarrow$(1) is trivial.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Abelian Galois group]
If $G$ is abelian, $\pi$ is injective and every fork is pinned: congruences determine every splitting question.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Universal non-pinning]\label{cor:never}
If $Y(gc) \ne Y(g)$ for some $g \in G$ and $c \in [G,G]$, then $I(\varphi;Y) \ne H(Y)$ for \emph{every} abelian character $\varphi$, of every conductor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Optimality of the abelianization]\label{thm:opt}
$I(\varphi;Y) \le I(\pi;Y)$ for every abelian character $\varphi$ and every $Y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\varphi = \tilde\varphi\circ\pi$; apply data processing.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conductor detection]\label{thm:cond}
$I(\varphi;Y) = I(\pi;Y)$ for every fork $Y : G \to \{0,1\}$ if and only if the induced map $\tilde\varphi : G^{\ab}\to A$ is injective, i.e.\ $\ker\varphi = [G,G]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If $\tilde\varphi$ is injective, $\varphi$ and $\pi$ have identical fibres. Otherwise choose $u\ne v$ with $\tilde\varphi(u)=\tilde\varphi(v)$ and let $Y$ be the indicator of $\pi^{-1}(u)$: then $I(\pi;Y) = H(Y) > 0$ while $\varphi$ does not determine $Y$, so strictness in Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(2) applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Flatness inside the commutator subgroup]\label{thm:flat}
Let $C = [G,G]$ with the uniform measure. For every abelian character $\varphi$ of $G$ and every $Y : C \to \beta$, $I(\varphi|_C; Y) = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\varphi$ is identically trivial on $C$, and a constant observable is independent of everything.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect groups are congruence-blind]\label{thm:perfect}
If $[G,G] = G$, then $I(\varphi;Y) = 0$ for every abelian character $\varphi$ and every $Y$; a pinned fork must be constant. This applies to $G = A_5$, since $A_5$ is simple and non-abelian, so $[A_5,A_5] = A_5$.
\end{theorem}

\section{Three Galois groups, with exact values}\label{sec:cases}

\subsection{Cyclic cubic fields: pinned at $100\%$}
Let $G = C_3$, realized by $f_1 = x^3+x^2-2x-1$ (conductor $7$) or $x^3-3x+1$ (conductor $9$). A Galois cubic admits only the splitting types $[1,1,1]$ and $[3]$; the type $[1,2]$ never occurs. The total-splitting fork is $Y(g) = [g = 0]$ on $\mathbb{Z}/3$, of density $1/3$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:c3}
$H(Y) = \log 3 - \tfrac23\log 2$ and $I(\mathrm{id};Y) = H(Y) = 0.9183$ bits: the fork is pinned at $100\%$ of its entropy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$H(Y) = \eta(1/3)+\eta(2/3) = \log3 - \tfrac23\log2$; the identity observable determines everything, so Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(2) applies.
\end{proof}

Arithmetically the cubic-residue character of conductor $7$ has image $C_3$ and trivial Frobenius exactly on $p \equiv \pm1 \pmod 7$; the measured information over $6541$ primes is $0.9182$ bits. Pinning persists at $m = 49$ ($42$ admissible classes with thousands of primes each), since a refinement of a pinning observable still pins; the coprime control $m = 5$ measures $0.0000$ bits, consistent with independence; and conductor $9$ behaves identically, with $[1,1,1] \iff p \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 9$ and measured $0.9181$ bits.

\subsection{The $S_3$ cubic: only the sign is pinned}
Let $f_2 = x^3+x+1$, $G = S_3$, $[G,G] = A_3$, $G^{\ab} = C_2$ generated by the sign --- the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-31})$. The total-splitting fork is $Y(\sigma) = [\sigma = 1]$, of density $1/6$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:s3}
With $X = \sgn$ on $S_3$,
\[
  H(Y) = \log2+\log3-\tfrac56\log5 = 0.6500 \text{ bits}, \qquad
  I(X;Y) = \tfrac43\log2+\tfrac12\log3-\tfrac56\log5 = 0.1909 \text{ bits},
\]
and $I(X;Y) = H(Y) - \tfrac12\bigl(\log 3 - \tfrac23\log 2\bigr)$. Moreover $0 < I(X;Y) < H(Y)$ strictly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The joint law is $\PR[\text{even},Y{=}1] = \tfrac16$, $\PR[\text{even},Y{=}0]=\tfrac13$, $\PR[\text{odd},Y{=}0]=\tfrac12$, $\PR[\text{odd},Y{=}1]=0$; substitute into $I = H(X)+H(Y)-H(X,Y)$. Non-determination is witnessed by the identity versus a $3$-cycle; positivity reduces to $2^8 3^3 = 6912 > 3125 = 5^5$.
\end{proof}

Measurement gives $0.1906$ bits and a beyond-sign residual of $+0.0000$: the congruence content of the fork is entirely the sign. On the quadratic-residue face, the $A_3$-fork ($[1,1,1]$ versus $[3]$) measures $0.0000$ bits, exactly as Theorem~\ref{thm:flat} requires.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:s3never}
The $S_3$ total-splitting fork is not commutator-invariant (take $g = 1$ and $c = [(0\,1),(1\,2)]$, a $3$-cycle), so by Corollary~\ref{cor:never} no abelian character of $S_3$, of any conductor, pins it. Furthermore $I(\sgn;Y_{S_3}) < I(\mathrm{id};Y_{C_3})$, which reduces to $110592 < 2278125$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Why the natural control failed]
The cubic $x^3-2$ has splitting field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]2,\sqrt{-3})$ with group $S_3$ and abelianization $C_2$, so its total-splitting fork is flat \emph{by construction}. Flatness is ``the fork lies outside $G^{\ab}$'', not ``the class number is $1$ rather than $3$''. The correct positive control is a cyclic cubic, which pins at $100\%$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The $S_4$ quartic: the sign is the only structure}
Let $f_4 = x^4-x-1$, of discriminant $-283$ (not a square), so $G = S_4$.

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-point counts]\label{thm:counts}
Among the $24$ elements of $S_4$, exactly $1$ has $4$ fixed points, $6$ have $2$, $8$ have $1$, and $9$ have $0$; so the number of roots of $f_4$ mod $p$ takes the values $4,2,1,0$ with densities $\tfrac1{24},\tfrac6{24},\tfrac8{24},\tfrac9{24}$.
\end{theorem}

Let $Y(\sigma) = [\sigma \text{ has a fixed point}]$, of density $15/24 = 5/8$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:s4}
With $X = \sgn$ on $S_4$,
\[
  H(Y) = 3\log2-\tfrac58\log5-\tfrac38\log3 = 0.9545 \text{ bits}, \qquad
  I(X;Y) = \tfrac32\log2-\tfrac58\log5 = 0.0488 \text{ bits},
\]
with $0 < I(X;Y) < H(Y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Among the $12$ even elements, the identity ($4$ fixed points) and the eight $3$-cycles ($1$ each) have a fixed point while the three double transpositions do not: $9$ out of $12$. Among the $12$ odd elements, the six transpositions have fixed points and the six $4$-cycles do not: $6$ out of $12$. Assemble the joint probabilities $\tfrac9{24},\tfrac3{24},\tfrac6{24},\tfrac6{24}$ and simplify. Positivity reduces to $2^{12} = 4096 > 3125 = 5^5$; the identity versus a double transposition witnesses non-determination.
\end{proof}

Measurement gives $0.0483$ bits. The beyond-sign residual $I(p \bmod 283;\ \text{has root}) - I(\sgn;\ \text{has root}) = +0.0131$ equals the conditional-null mean exactly, i.e.\ finite-sample bias with no signal, and every within-face fork (even: $[1,1,1,1]$, $[2,2]$, $[1,3]$; odd: $[1,1,2]$, $[4]$) measures its null mean. This is forced by Theorem~\ref{thm:flat}, the even face being $A_4 = [S_4,S_4]$. As in Theorem~\ref{thm:s3never}, the has-a-root fork is not commutator-invariant, so no abelian character pins it.

\section{The capacity of a binary fork}\label{sec:cap}

\begin{theorem}[Strict maximum entropy]\label{thm:maxent}
For a fork $Y$ with $\PR[Y=1] = q$, $H(Y) \le \log 2$ with equality iff $q = \tfrac12$, and $H(Y) < \log 2$ strictly otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Termwise, $\eta(t) - t\log 2 \le \tfrac12 - t$ for $t \ge 0$, strictly unless $t = \tfrac12$; this follows from the strict inequality $\log u < u - 1$ for $u \ne 1$ applied to $u = 1/(2t)$, with $t = 0$ checked separately. Sum over $t = q$ and $t = 1-q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One-bit ceiling and exact attainment]\label{thm:cap}
For any observable $X$ and any fork $Y$, $I(X;Y) \le \log 2$; and
\[
  I(X;Y) = \log 2 \iff X \text{ determines } Y \text{ and } Y \text{ is balanced.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$I \le H(Y) \le \log 2$. If $I = \log 2$ then $H(Y) = \log 2$, so $Y$ is balanced by Theorem~\ref{thm:maxent} and $I = H(Y)$ gives determination by Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(2); the converse is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Surjective characters are uniform]\label{lem:unif}
If $\varphi : G \to A$ is a surjective homomorphism of finite groups with $G$ uniform, then $\PR[\varphi = a] = 1/|A|$ for all $a \in A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Left translation by any $g_0$ with $\varphi(g_0) = ba^{-1}$ is a bijection from the fibre over $a$ to the fibre over $b$; equal fibre probabilities summing to $1$ are each $1/|A|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For $n \ge 2$, $\PR[\sgn = +1] = \tfrac12$ on $S_n$, since $\sgn$ is surjective onto $\{\pm1\}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity in the symmetric group]\label{thm:rigid}
For $n \ge 2$ and a fork $Y$ of $S_n$,
\[
  I(\sgn;Y) = \log 2 \iff Y = \sgn \ \text{ or } \ Y = \neg\,\sgn .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Both candidates are sign-determined and balanced. Conversely, Theorem~\ref{thm:cap} forces $Y$ to be sign-determined and balanced; determination gives $Y(\sigma) = Y(1)$ for even $\sigma$ and $Y(\sigma) = Y(\tau)$ for odd $\sigma$ with $\tau$ a fixed transposition, leaving four candidates, of which balance eliminates the two constants.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid} is the exact counterpart of the measurement that the only congruence structure in the whole $S_4$ splitting is the sign.

\section{The extremal profile of an index-two conductor}\label{sec:profile}

\begin{definition}
With $h(t) = \eta(t)+\eta(1-t)$ the binary entropy, the \emph{coset profile} is
\[
  \Phi(d) = h(d) - \tfrac12 h(2d) = d\log 2 - (1-d)\log(1-d) + \tfrac12(1-2d)\log(1-2d),
  \qquad 0 \le d \le \tfrac12 .
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Extremality]\label{thm:extremal}
If $X$ is a balanced fork and $Y$ a fork of density $d = \PR[Y=1] \le \tfrac12$, then $I(X;Y) \le \Phi(d)$, with equality whenever the support of $Y$ lies in a single fibre of $X$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For balanced $X$, $I(X;Y) = h(d) - \tfrac12(h(a)+h(b))$ where $a,b$ are the conditional densities in the two fibres and $a+b = 2d$. Subadditivity $h(a+b) \le h(a)+h(b)$ gives the bound; equality occurs when one of $a,b$ vanishes, i.e.\ for single-coset forks.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Properties of the profile]\label{thm:profile}
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Phi \ge 0$ and $\Phi$ is strictly increasing on $[0,\tfrac12]$.
\item $\Phi(\tfrac12) = \log 2$.
\item $|\Phi(d) - d\log 2| \le 4d^2$ for $0 < d \le \tfrac14$; hence $\Phi(d)/d \to \log 2$ as $d \to 0^+$.
\item $\Phi(d)/h(d) \le \dfrac{\log2 + 4d}{\log(1/d)}$ for $0 < d \le \tfrac14$; hence $\Phi(d)/h(d)\to 0$ as $d\to0^+$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) Nonnegativity is subadditivity; the derivative is $\Phi'(d) = \log\frac{2(1-d)}{1-2d} > 0$. (2) $h(1) = 0$. (3) Apply $|\log(1-x)+x+x^2/2| \le 2x^3$ for $0 \le x \le \tfrac12$ at $x = d$ and $x = 2d$; the linear terms cancel against $d\log2$ and the remainders total at most $4d^2$. (4) Divide (3) by $h(d) \ge d\log(1/d)$.
\end{proof}

Item (4) corrects a natural guess: the small-$d$ behaviour is $d\log 2$, not $d\log(1/d)$, and the pinned fraction of a rare fork's entropy tends to $0$, not to $\tfrac12$.

\section{The semiprime barrier}\label{sec:semi}

Let $N = pq$, so that the model supplies independent uniform $g_1,g_2 \in G$; the observable is $S = g_1g_2$ and the fork is $\OR(g_1,g_2) = [g_1 = 1 \text{ or } g_2 = 1]$.

\begin{theorem}[Universal semiprime dial]\label{thm:dial}
For any finite $G$ with $n = |G| \ge 2$,
\[
  I(S;\OR) = D(n) := \log n + \frac{-(2n-1)\log(2n-1) + (n-1)(3-2n)\log(n-1) + 2(n-1)\log 2 + (n-1)(n-2)\log(n-2)}{n^2}.
\]
In particular the answer depends only on the order of $G$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$S$ is uniform, since $g_2 \mapsto g_1g_2$ is a bijection, so $H(S) = \log n$. For each $s$ the fibre $\{(g_1,g_2): g_1g_2 = s\}$ has $n$ elements, of which the $\OR$-true ones are $(1,s)$ and $(s,1)$: two if $s \ne 1$, one if $s = 1$. Hence $\PR[\OR] = (2n-1)/n^2$, and the joint cells are $\tfrac1{n^2}, \tfrac{n-1}{n^2}$ over $s = 1$ and $\tfrac2{n^2}, \tfrac{n-2}{n^2}$ over each $s \ne 1$. Substituting into $I = H(S)+H(\OR)-H(S,\OR)$ gives the formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For $|G| = 3$, $I(S;\OR) = \log 3 - \tfrac59\log5 - \tfrac29\log2 = 0.0728$ bits, with $\PR[\OR \mid S = 1] = 1/3$ and $\PR[\OR \mid S \ne 1] = 2/3$; the measured value for the conductor-$7$ cyclic cubic was $0.0718$ bits.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic collapse]\label{thm:collapse}
For $n \ge 2$, $I(S;\OR) \le \dfrac{1}{(2n-1)(n-1)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Bound $I$ by the $\chi^2$-divergence $\sum_{k,b}\PR[(X,Y)=(k,b)]^2/(\PR[X=k]\PR[Y=b]) - 1$, which follows from $\log t \le t-1$ termwise, and evaluate on the explicit joint law of Theorem~\ref{thm:dial}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp constant]\label{thm:sharp}
$n^2D(n) \to 1 - \log 2 = 0.30685\ldots$ as $n \to \infty$, with $|n^2D(n) - (1-\log2)| \le 24/n$ for $n \ge 4$. Moreover $n^2D(n) < 1$ for every $n \ge 2$, and $4D(2) = 3\log(4/3) = 0.8630$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Expanding around $\log n$, the leading terms cancel identically and
\[
  n^2D(n) = -\log2 - (2n-1)\log\Bigl(1-\tfrac1{2n}\Bigr) + (n-1)(3-2n)\log\Bigl(1-\tfrac1n\Bigr) + (n-1)(n-2)\log\Bigl(1-\tfrac2n\Bigr).
\]
Apply $|\log(1-x)+x+x^2/2| \le 2x^3$ to each logarithm; first- and second-order terms combine to $1 - \log 2$ and the remainders are $O(1/n)$ with constant $24$. The uniform bound $n^2D(n) < 1$ follows from the exact value at $n = 2$, the tail estimate for $n \ge 4$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse} in between.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Which-factor wall]\label{thm:wall}
For any statistic $F : G \to \beta$ of the first factor alone, $I(S; F(g_1)) = 0$ exactly. More generally, for $P = g_1\cdots g_{k+1}$ and any statistic $F$ of $(g_1,\dots,g_k)$, $I(P; F) = 0$, and $P$ is uniform.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Conditioned on $g_1$, the product $g_1g_2$ is uniform on $G$, hence independent of $g_1$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(3). The $k$-factor case follows by re-associating $P = (g_1\cdots g_k)g_{k+1}$ and using invariance of mutual information under the bijection $G^k \times G \cong G^{k+1}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
For $|G| \ge 2$, $0 < I(S;\OR) < H(\OR)$: the semiprime dial is a genuine but strictly partial signal.
\end{theorem}

Thus a prime-level fork pinned at $100\%$ becomes, at the semiprime level, a symmetric $0.0728$-bit dial for $n = 3$; the dial is universal in $n$, decays like $(1-\log2)/n^2$ with hard budget $n^2I < 1$, and is provably orthogonal to the question of which factor is which. Measurement agreed, with a which-factor information of $0.0001$ bits.

\section{Algorithms}

\textbf{A. Commutator-invariance pinning test.} Given generators of $G$ and a fork $Y$, enumerate $G$, compute $[G,G]$ as the closure under the generated commutators, and test constancy of $Y$ on each coset $g[G,G]$; cost $O(|G|\cdot|\text{gens}|)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:crit} this decides pinning against all abelian characters at once --- no search over moduli is needed --- and returns a witness $(g,c)$ on failure.

\textbf{B. Exact fork information.} Build the joint histogram of $(X,Y)$ over $G$ in one pass, $O(|G|)$, and evaluate $H(Y)$, $I(X;Y)$ and the pinned fraction $I/H$.

\textbf{C. Universal dial evaluation.} Evaluate $D(n)$ in constant time by Theorem~\ref{thm:dial}; for large $n$ prefer the expansion $D(n) = (1-\log2)/n^2 + O(1/n^3)$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp}, the closed form suffering catastrophic cancellation between $\log n$ terms.

An empirical companion verifies the model on primes: count roots of $f$ modulo each $p$ (by $\gcd(f, x^p - x)$, or naively in $O(p)$), classify the splitting type, and compare the empirical joint law with the group prediction.

\section{Applications and discussion}

\emph{Deciding predictability without searching moduli.} To know that no congruence rule exists, one computes the abelianization and checks whether the fork descends; a single commutator witness rules out all conductors at once.

\emph{Designing controls.} The choice of a positive control in an experimental study of splitting statistics must be made by the criterion, not by superficial invariants: class number, discriminant size and regulator are irrelevant; only factorization through $G^{\ab}$ matters.

\emph{Cryptographic non-implications.} Section~\ref{sec:semi} closes the route from splitting data to factoring quantitatively: the total information at the semiprime level is $D(n) < 1/n^2$ nats for every field, it is symmetric in the two factors, and the wall persists for multi-factor moduli.

\emph{A general principle.} Any measurement channel factoring through a commutative quotient is blind to the commutator subgroup. Where a hidden state is a random group element and the measurement is an abelian character, the answerable questions are exactly the functions on the abelianization, and the abelianization is the canonical optimal measurement, characterized by its kernel.

\section{Future work}

Open questions include: a \emph{conductor hierarchy} organizing intermediate characters into a unique minimal pinning quotient for a fixed fork; a $\log n/n^2$ \emph{information budget} for arbitrary factorization oracles built from splitting data across several fields simultaneously; \emph{monotonicity} of $n^2D(n)$, numerically decreasing from $3\log(4/3)$ to $1-\log2$; the \emph{multi-factor dial}, conjectured to decay like $k^2/n^2$; \emph{non-uniform priors}, where conditioning on congruence conditions makes the induced measure uniform on a coset; and the \emph{$r$-valued capacity profile}, where the ceiling is $\log r$ and the attainment condition should read ``determined and uniform''.

    <=>  factors through the abelianization.  Decided by direct enumeration.

        x^3 + x + 1        has no congruence rule; only the sign is visible
        x^4 - x - 1        root counts 4:2:1:0 in ratio 1:6:8:9 out of 24
4.  Capacity: I <= log 2 for any binary fork, attained exactly at balanced
    pinned forks; in S_n only by the sign and its negation.
5.  The coset profile  Phi(d) = h(d) - h(2d)/2: sharp bound for an
    index-two conductor, strictly increasing, Phi(d)/d -> log 2,
    Phi(d)/h(d) -> 0.

    n^2 D(n) -> 1 - log 2 = 0.30685, and the exactly-zero which-factor wall.

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]

LOG2 = math.log(2.0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Information theory on a finite uniform space
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def eta(t: float) -> float:
    """-t log t, with eta(0) = 0."""
    return 0.0 if t <= 0.0 else -t * math.log(t)


def entropy(values: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    """Entropy (nats) of the empirical law of a list of outcomes."""
    n = len(values)
    counts: Dict[object, int] = {}
    for v in values:
        counts[v] = counts.get(v, 0) + 1
    return sum(eta(c / n) for c in counts.values())


def mutual_information(xs: Sequence[object], ys: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    """I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y) in nats, for paired samples."""
    return entropy(xs) + entropy(ys) - entropy(list(zip(xs, ys)))


def bits(nats: float) -> float:
    return nats / LOG2


def binary_entropy(d: float) -> float:
    return eta(d) + eta(1.0 - d)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Permutation groups as explicit lists of tuples
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    return [tuple(p) for p in itertools.permutations(range(n))]


def compose(a: Perm, b: Perm) -> Perm:
    """(a*b)(i) = a(b(i))."""
    return tuple(a[b[i]] for i in range(len(a)))


def inverse(a: Perm) -> Perm:
    out = [0] * len(a)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        out[ai] = i
    return tuple(out)


def sign(a: Perm) -> int:
    """+1 or -1, computed from the parity of the number of transpositions."""
    seen = [False] * len(a)
    parity = 0
    for i in range(len(a)):
        if not seen[i]:
            j, length = i, 0
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = a[j]
                length += 1
            parity += length - 1
    return 1 if parity % 2 == 0 else -1


def alternating_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    return [p for p in symmetric_group(n) if sign(p) == 1]


def cycle_type(a: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    seen = [False] * len(a)
    parts: List[int] = []
    for i in range(len(a)):
        if not seen[i]:
            j, length = i, 0
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = a[j]
                length += 1
            parts.append(length)
    return tuple(sorted(parts))


def commutator_subgroup(group: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """Subgroup generated by all commutators [g,h] = g h g^-1 h^-1."""
    gens = {compose(compose(g, h), compose(inverse(g), inverse(h)))
            for g in group for h in group}
    identity = tuple(range(len(group[0])))
    closure = {identity}
    frontier = [identity]
    while frontier:
        x = frontier.pop()
        for s in gens:
            y = compose(x, s)
            if y not in closure:
                closure.add(y)
                frontier.append(y)
    return sorted(closure)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fork-pinning criterion, decided by enumeration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_commutator_invariant(group: Sequence[Perm],
                            fork: Callable[[Perm], bool]
                            ) -> Tuple[bool, Tuple[Perm, Perm] | None]:
    """Test Y(g c) = Y(g) for all g in G, c in [G,G]; return a witness if not."""
    comm = commutator_subgroup(group)
    for g in group:
        for c in comm:
            if fork(compose(g, c)) != fork(g):
                return False, (g, c)
    return True, None


def fork_report(name: str,
                group: Sequence[Perm],
                observable: Callable[[Perm], object],
                fork: Callable[[Perm], bool],
                closed_form: float | None = None) -> None:
    xs = [observable(g) for g in group]
    ys = [fork(g) for g in group]
    h_y = entropy(ys)
    info = mutual_information(xs, ys)
    pinned_fraction = info / h_y if h_y > 0 else float("nan")
    invariant, witness = is_commutator_invariant(group, fork)
    print(f"  {name}")
    print(f"     P[fork] = {sum(ys)}/{len(ys)} = {sum(ys)/len(ys):.6f}")
    print(f"     H(fork) = {bits(h_y):.6f} bits")
    print(f"     I(obs;fork) = {bits(info):.6f} bits", end="")
    if closed_form is not None:
        print(f"   (closed form {bits(closed_form):.6f} bits,"
              f" |diff| = {abs(bits(info) - bits(closed_form)):.2e})")

def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i::i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i::i]))
    return [i for i in range(limit + 1) if sieve[i]]


def count_roots_mod_p(coeffs: Sequence[int], p: int) -> int:
    """Number of x in F_p with sum coeffs[i] x^i = 0 (coeffs in ascending degree)."""
    total = 0
    for x in range(p):
        acc = 0
        xp = 1
        for c in coeffs:
            acc = (acc + c * xp) % p
            xp = (xp * x) % p
        if acc == 0:
            total += 1
    return total


def demo_primes(limit: int = 60000) -> None:

def coset_profile(d: float) -> float:
    """Phi(d) = h(d) - h(2d)/2, the sharp bound for a balanced observable."""
    return binary_entropy(d) - binary_entropy(2 * d) / 2

def semiprime_dial(n: float) -> float:
    """Closed form D(n) of the semiprime-level mutual information (nats)."""
    return math.log(n) + (
        -(2 * n - 1) * math.log(2 * n - 1)
        + (n - 1) * (3 - 2 * n) * math.log(n - 1)
        + 2 * (n - 1) * LOG2
        + ((n - 1) * (n - 2) * math.log(n - 2) if n > 2 else 0.0)
    ) / (n * n)

        ("S3", symmetric_group(3), compose, (0, 1, 2)),
        ("C4", [0, 1, 2, 3], lambda a, b: (a + b) % 4, 0),
        ("S4", symmetric_group(4), compose, (0, 1, 2, 3)),

        pairs = [(a, b) for a in group for b in group]
        classes = [mul(a, b) for a, b in pairs]

        first = [a for a, _ in pairs]

        print(f"     WHICH-FACTOR WALL  I(class of N ; first factor) = {bits(i_which):.3e} bits"
              f"   (exactly 0)")

    print("\n   Universal dial and the sharp constant  n^2 D(n) -> 1 - log 2 = "

    # The k-factor wall.
    print("\n   k-factor wall (products of k+1 uniform elements of C3):")

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]

LOG2 = math.log(2.0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Information theory on a finite uniform space
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def eta(t: float) -> float:
    """-t log t, with eta(0) = 0."""
    return 0.0 if t <= 0.0 else -t * math.log(t)


def entropy(values: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    """Entropy (nats) of the empirical law of a list of outcomes."""
    n = len(values)
    counts: Dict[object, int] = {}
    for v in values:
        counts[v] = counts.get(v, 0) + 1
    return sum(eta(c / n) for c in counts.values())


def mutual_information(xs: Sequence[object], ys: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    """I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y) in nats, for paired samples."""
    return entropy(xs) + entropy(ys) - entropy(list(zip(xs, ys)))


def bits(nats: float) -> float:
    return nats / LOG2


def binary_entropy(d: float) -> float:
    return eta(d) + eta(1.0 - d)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Permutation groups as explicit lists of tuples
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    return [tuple(p) for p in itertools.permutations(range(n))]


def compose(a: Perm, b: Perm) -> Perm:
    """(a*b)(i) = a(b(i))."""
    return tuple(a[b[i]] for i in range(len(a)))


def inverse(a: Perm) -> Perm:
    out = [0] * len(a)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        out[ai] = i
    return tuple(out)


def sign(a: Perm) -> int:
    """+1 or -1, computed from the parity of the number of transpositions."""
    seen = [False] * len(a)
    parity = 0
    for i in range(len(a)):
        if not seen[i]:
            j, length = i, 0
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = a[j]
                length += 1
            parity += length - 1
    return 1 if parity % 2 == 0 else -1


def alternating_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    return [p for p in symmetric_group(n) if sign(p) == 1]


def cycle_type(a: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    seen = [False] * len(a)
    parts: List[int] = []
    for i in range(len(a)):
        if not seen[i]:
            j, length = i, 0
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = a[j]
                length += 1
            parts.append(length)
    return tuple(sorted(parts))


def commutator_subgroup(group: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """Subgroup generated by all commutators [g,h] = g h g^-1 h^-1."""
    gens = {compose(compose(g, h), compose(inverse(g), inverse(h)))
            for g in group for h in group}
    identity = tuple(range(len(group[0])))
    closure = {identity}
    frontier = [identity]
    while frontier:
        x = frontier.pop()
        for s in gens:
            y = compose(x, s)
            if y not in closure:
                closure.add(y)
                frontier.append(y)
    return sorted(closure)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fork-pinning criterion, decided by enumeration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_commutator_invariant(group: Sequence[Perm],
                            fork: Callable[[Perm], bool]
                            ) -> Tuple[bool, Tuple[Perm, Perm] | None]:
    """Test Y(g c) = Y(g) for all g in G, c in [G,G]; return a witness if not."""
    comm = commutator_subgroup(group)
    for g in group:
        for c in comm:
            if fork(compose(g, c)) != fork(g):
                return False, (g, c)
    return True, None


def fork_report(name: str,
                group: Sequence[Perm],
                observable: Callable[[Perm], object],
                fork: Callable[[Perm], bool],
                closed_form: float | None = None) -> None:
    xs = [observable(g) for g in group]
    ys = [fork(g) for g in group]
    h_y = entropy(ys)
    info = mutual_information(xs, ys)
    pinned_fraction = info / h_y if h_y > 0 else float("nan")

def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i::i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i::i]))
    return [i for i in range(limit + 1) if sieve[i]]


def count_roots_mod_p(coeffs: Sequence[int], p: int) -> int:
    """Number of x in F_p with sum coeffs[i] x^i = 0 (coeffs in ascending degree)."""
    total = 0
    for x in range(p):
        acc = 0
        xp = 1
        for c in coeffs:
            acc = (acc + c * xp) % p
            xp = (xp * x) % p
        if acc == 0:
            total += 1
    return total

def coset_profile(d: float) -> float:
    """Phi(d) = h(d) - h(2d)/2, the sharp bound for a balanced observable."""
    return binary_entropy(d) - binary_entropy(2 * d) / 2


def demo_profile() -> None:

def semiprime_dial(n: float) -> float:
    """Closed form D(n) of the semiprime-level mutual information (nats)."""
    return math.log(n) + (
        -(2 * n - 1) * math.log(2 * n - 1)
        + (n - 1) * (3 - 2 * n) * math.log(n - 1)
        + 2 * (n - 1) * LOG2
        + ((n - 1) * (n - 2) * math.log(n - 2) if n > 2 else 0.0)
    ) / (n * n)

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

LOG2 = math.log(2.0)


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i::i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i::i]))
    return [i for i in range(limit + 1) if sieve[i]]


def count_roots_mod_p(coeffs: Sequence[int], p: int) -> int:
    total = 0
    for x in range(p):
        acc, xp = 0, 1
        for c in coeffs:
            acc = (acc + c * xp) % p
            xp = (xp * x) % p
        if acc == 0:
            total += 1
    return total


def eta(t: float) -> float:
    return 0.0 if t <= 0 else -t * math.log(t)


def entropy(vals: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    counts: Dict[object, int] = {}
    for v in vals:
        counts[v] = counts.get(v, 0) + 1
    return sum(eta(c / len(vals)) for c in counts.values())


def mutual_information(xs: Sequence[object], ys: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    return entropy(xs) + entropy(ys) - entropy(list(zip(xs, ys)))


def mine(coeffs: Sequence[int], label: str, m_max: int = 60,
         limit: int = 30000) -> None:
    ps = [p for p in primes_up_to(limit) if p > 5]
    forks = [count_roots_mod_p(coeffs, p) == len(coeffs) - 1 for p in ps]
    print(f"\n{label}:  {len(ps)} primes, density of total splitting"
          f" = {sum(forks)/len(forks):.5f}")
    print("    m    best rule accuracy    I(p mod m ; fork) [bits]   exact rule?")
    best_overall: Tuple[float, int, Set[int]] = (0.0, 0, set())
    for m in range(3, m_max + 1):
        good = [(p % m, f) for p, f in zip(ps, forks) if math.gcd(p, m) == 1]
        if not good:
            continue
        classes = sorted({r for r, _ in good})
        # the optimal rule takes each class to its majority label
        stats = {c: [0, 0] for c in classes}
        for r, f in good:
            stats[r][1 if f else 0] += 1
        chosen: Set[int] = {c for c in classes if stats[c][1] >= stats[c][0]}
        correct = sum(stats[c][1] if c in chosen else stats[c][0] for c in classes)
        acc = correct / len(good)
        info = mutual_information([r for r, _ in good], [f for _, f in good])
        exact = all(stats[c][0] == 0 or stats[c][1] == 0 for c in classes)

        if m <= 12 or exact or m in (31, 49, 59, 60):

                  f"              {'YES  S = ' + str(sorted(chosen)) if exact else 'no'}")
    acc, m, chosen = best_overall
    print(f"   best over all moduli tested: m = {m}, accuracy {acc:.6f},"
          f" classes {sorted(chosen)}")

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]


def compose(a: Perm, b: Perm) -> Perm:

def inverse(a: Perm) -> Perm:
    out = [0] * len(a)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        out[ai] = i
    return tuple(out)


def commutator_subgroup(group: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """[G,G] as the subgroup generated by all commutators g h g^-1 h^-1."""
    gens = {compose(compose(g, h), compose(inverse(g), inverse(h)))
            for g in group for h in group}

                stack.append(y)
    return sorted(closure)

import math
from typing import Dict

LOG2 = math.log(2.0)


def semiprime_dial_closed(n: float) -> float:
    """Exact closed form, in nats."""
    tail = (n - 1) * (n - 2) * math.log(n - 2) if n > 2 else 0.0
    return math.log(n) + (
        -(2 * n - 1) * math.log(2 * n - 1)
        + (n - 1) * (3 - 2 * n) * math.log(n - 1)
        + 2 * (n - 1) * LOG2
        + tail
    ) / (n * n)


def scaled_dial_stable(n: float) -> float:
    """n^2 D(n) written with the log n terms cancelled analytically."""
    return (-LOG2
            - (2 * n - 1) * math.log1p(-1 / (2 * n))
            + (n - 1) * (3 - 2 * n) * math.log1p(-1 / n)
            + (n - 1) * (n - 2) * math.log1p(-2 / n))


def semiprime_dial(n: float) -> float:
    """Numerically robust value of D(n) in nats."""
    return semiprime_dial_closed(n) if n < 1e4 else scaled_dial_stable(n) / (n * n)

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

LOG2 = math.log(2.0)


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i::i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i::i]))
    return [i for i in range(limit + 1) if sieve[i]]


def count_roots_mod_p(coeffs: Sequence[int], p: int) -> int:
    """Roots in F_p of sum coeffs[i] x^i (coefficients in ascending degree)."""
    total = 0
    for x in range(p):
        acc, xp = 0, 1
        for c in coeffs:
            acc = (acc + c * xp) % p
            xp = (xp * x) % p
        if acc == 0:
            total += 1
    return total


def eta(t: float) -> float:
    return 0.0 if t <= 0 else -t * math.log(t)


def entropy(vals: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    counts: Dict[object, int] = {}
    for v in vals:
        counts[v] = counts.get(v, 0) + 1
    return sum(eta(c / len(vals)) for c in counts.values())


def mutual_information(xs: Sequence[object], ys: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    return entropy(xs) + entropy(ys) - entropy(list(zip(xs, ys)))

                           fork: Callable[[int], bool],

                           good_classes: Set[int],

    ps = [p for p in primes_up_to(limit) if p > modulus and p % modulus != 0]

        "exceptions": float(exceptions),
        "density": sum(forks) / len(forks),
        "I_bits": info / LOG2,
        "H_bits": h / LOG2,
        "pinned_fraction": info / h if h > 0 else float("nan"),
    }

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

LOG2 = math.log(2.0)


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i::i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i::i]))
    return [i for i in range(limit + 1) if sieve[i]]


def count_roots(coeffs: Sequence[int], p: int) -> int:
    total = 0
    for x in range(p):
        acc, xp = 0, 1
        for c in coeffs:
            acc = (acc + c * xp) % p
            xp = (xp * x) % p
        if acc == 0:
            total += 1
    return total


def eta(t: float) -> float:
    return 0.0 if t <= 0 else -t * math.log(t)


def entropy(vals: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    counts: Dict[object, int] = {}
    for v in vals:
        counts[v] = counts.get(v, 0) + 1
    n = len(vals)
    return sum(eta(c / n) for c in counts.values())


def mutual_information(xs: Sequence[object], ys: Sequence[object]) -> float:
    return entropy(xs) + entropy(ys) - entropy(list(zip(xs, ys)))


def main(limit: int = 40000) -> None:
    ps = [p for p in primes_up_to(limit) if p > 5]

    axes[1].set_ylim(0, 0.45)
    axes[1].legend(fontsize=9)

    # panel 3
    names = ["cyclic cubic\n(mod 7)", "$S_3$ cubic\n(sign)", "$S_4$ quartic\n(sign)"]

    axes[2].grid(alpha=.25, axis="y")

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("pinned_vs_flat.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote pinned_vs_flat.png")

*A guided tour of the fork-pinning criterion: from a spooky pattern in the primes to an exact information-theoretic dichotomy.*

---

## 1. A pattern that should not be there

Take the cubic polynomial $x^3 + x^2 - 2x - 1$ and reduce it modulo a prime $p$. Sometimes it splits into three linear factors; sometimes it stays irreducible. Which is it? Here are the first few answers:

| $p$ | 11 | 13 | 17 | 19 | 23 | 29 | 31 | 41 | 43 | 71 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| splits? | no | **yes** | no | no | no | **yes** | no | **yes** | **yes** | **yes** |
| $p \bmod 7$ | 4 | **6** | 3 | 5 | 2 | **1** | 3 | **6** | **1** | **1** |

The splitters are exactly the primes $\equiv \pm 1 \pmod 7$. Across the first several thousand primes there is **not one exception**.

Now try the same game with $x^3 + x + 1$. Search every modulus you like. You will never find a rule. This notebook explains — precisely, and with an exact information-theoretic accounting — why one polynomial is transparent and the other is opaque forever.

<details>
<summary><b>Background: what does "splitting type" mean?</b> (click to expand)</summary>

For a monic $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $n$ and a prime $p$ not dividing the discriminant, the reduction $f \bmod p$ factors into distinct irreducible polynomials over the field $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $p$ elements. Their degrees form a partition of $n$, called the **splitting type** of $p$. For a cubic the options are $[1,1,1]$ (three roots), $[1,2]$ (one root and an irreducible quadratic), and $[3]$ (irreducible). Testing for $[1,1,1]$ is easy: count roots in $\mathbb{F}_p$.

More on the underlying theory: [splitting of prime ideals in Galois extensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splitting_of_prime_ideals_in_Galois_extensions).
</details>

---

## 2. The dictionary: primes become group elements

Two classical theorems turn this into finite group theory.

**Chebotarev's density theorem (1922).** Let $L$ be the splitting field of $f$ and $G$ its group of symmetries, acting on the $n$ roots. Then a prime drawn by natural density behaves as a **uniformly random element $g \in G$**, and the splitting type of $p$ is the cycle type of $g$.

**Abelian reciprocity.** A congruence condition on $p$ sees exactly the **abelian characters** of $G$ — homomorphisms $\varphi : G \to A$ into commutative groups. Every such map kills all commutators $[g,h] = ghg^{-1}h^{-1}$ and so factors through the **abelianization**
$$G^{\mathrm{ab}} = G/[G,G].$$

So: congruences are *abelian eyes*. They can see only the commutative shadow of the Galois group.

<details>
<summary><b>Why does a congruence correspond to an abelian character?</b></summary>

The residue $p \bmod m$ is the Frobenius of $p$ in the cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$, whose Galois group $(\mathbb{Z}/m)^\times$ is abelian. Asking whether a splitting fact is determined by $p \bmod m$ is asking whether it is determined by the image of the Frobenius in an abelian quotient. See [Chebotarev's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chebotarev%27s_density_theorem) and [Artin reciprocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artin_reciprocity_law).
</details>

---

## 3. Play with the criterion

A **fork** is any yes/no question about the splitting type. The central result of this work is:

> **The fork-pinning criterion.** A fork is determined by some congruence condition **if and only if** it factors through the abelianization of the Galois group — equivalently, if and only if $Y(gc) = Y(g)$ for every group element $g$ and every commutator $c$.

There is no partial credit at the top. Either the fork descends to $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ and some congruence settles it exactly, or no modulus — however astronomically large — ever will.

Try it yourself. Start with $C_3$ (a cyclic cubic field, abelian group) and any fork: everything pins. Then switch to $S_4$ and the fork "has a root": watch the witness appear — an explicit pair $(g, c)$ with $Y(gc) \ne Y(g)$ that single-handedly rules out every modulus at once. Finally choose $A_5$: a perfect group, whose abelianization is trivial, so *every* fork is flat.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

<details>
<summary><b>Proof sketch of the criterion</b></summary>

Two ingredients. First, on a finite uniform probability space, "pinned" and "determined" coincide: $I(X;Y) = H(Y)$ if and only if $X$ determines $Y$ pointwise. (Write $H(X,Y) - H(X) = \sum_k \Pr[X=k]\,H(Y \mid X = k)$; this is zero exactly when every fibre of $X$ carries a single value of $Y$.)

Second, any abelian character $\varphi$ factors as $\tilde\varphi \circ \pi$ through the abelianization map $\pi$. So if $\varphi$ determines $Y$, then so does $\pi$ — and determination by $\pi$ is exactly constancy on cosets of $[G,G]$, i.e. commutator invariance. Conversely, if $Y$ is commutator-invariant then $\pi$ itself pins it.

A bonus: the abelianization is **optimal**. Because $\varphi = \tilde\varphi \circ \pi$ and post-processing never increases information, $I(\varphi;Y) \le I(\pi;Y)$ for every abelian character, and equality holds for *all* forks precisely when $\ker\varphi = [G,G]$.
</details>

---

## 4. The numbers, exactly

Theory is one thing; the primes are another. Here are the three fields side by side, with the exact values against the measurements.

| field | Galois group | $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ | fork | exact $I$ | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $x^3+x^2-2x-1$ | $C_3$ | $C_3$ | splits completely | $\log 3 - \tfrac23\log2 = 0.9183$ bits | $0.9182$ |
| $x^3+x+1$ | $S_3$ | $C_2$ | splits completely | $\tfrac43\log2+\tfrac12\log3-\tfrac56\log5 = 0.1909$ | $0.1906$ |
| $x^4-x-1$ | $S_4$ | $C_2$ | has a root | $\tfrac32\log2-\tfrac58\log5 = 0.0488$ | $0.0483$ |

For the cyclic cubic the information equals the fork's whole entropy: $100\%$ pinned. For the other two, the visible bit is the *sign* of the Frobenius permutation — a classical Jacobi symbol — and nothing else survives.

{{visualization:1}}

<details>

In $S_3$ the fork "$\sigma = 1$" has probability $1/6$, and the only element making it true is even. So the joint law is $\tfrac16, \tfrac13, \tfrac12, 0$, giving
$$I = \tfrac43\log2+\tfrac12\log3-\tfrac56\log5, \qquad H = \log2+\log3-\tfrac56\log5,$$
and subtracting, $I = H - \tfrac12\big(\log 3 - \tfrac23\log 2\big) = H - \tfrac12 H(1/3)$. The unresolved half-entropy is exactly the $A_3$ part of the group: the piece congruences cannot see.
</details>

## 5. An exhaustive search that is guaranteed to fail

The criterion makes a strong empirical prediction: for $x^3+x+1$, brute-force searching *every* modulus for an exact rule must fail, and the information must saturate at the sign's $0.1909$ bits. Run the miner and watch it happen — success at $m = 7$ (and every multiple of $7$) for the cyclic cubic, permanent failure for the $S_3$ cubic.

## 6. How much is a yes/no question worth at most?

Once we know *whether* a fork can be pinned, we can ask how much information any observable extracts. The answer is a hard ceiling of one bit, with an exact attainment condition.

> **Capacity theorem.** For any observable $X$ and any binary fork $Y$, $I(X;Y) \le \log 2$, with equality **iff** $X$ determines $Y$ *and* $Y$ is balanced.

> **Rigidity in $S_n$.** Among all binary forks of the symmetric group, the one-bit capacity is attained by **exactly two**: the sign and its negation.

That is the formal counterpart of the experimental verdict on the $S_4$ quartic — the only congruence structure in the entire splitting behaviour is the sign.

<details>
<summary><b>Why balance is forced</b></summary>

A two-valued statistic has $H(Y) = \log 2$ if and only if it is balanced; otherwise $H(Y) < \log 2$ strictly. (Termwise, $\eta(t) - t\log 2 \le \tfrac12 - t$ with equality only at $t = \tfrac12$, from the strict inequality $\log u < u - 1$.) Since $I \le H(Y) \le \log 2$, hitting the ceiling forces both $H(Y) = \log2$ — balance — and $I = H(Y)$ — determination.
</details>

There is a graded version for rare events. If the visible observable is one balanced bit and the fork has density $d \le \tfrac12$, then
$$I \le \Phi(d) = h(d) - \tfrac12 h(2d),$$
sharply, with equality exactly for forks living inside a single coset. Slide $d$ below and watch the two competing effects: $\Phi$ is strictly increasing (rarer is strictly harder), grows linearly like $d\log 2$, and yet the *fraction* of the fork's entropy that gets pinned collapses to zero.

{{interactive_demo:2}}

## 7. Why this does not break cryptography

Tempting thought: use a $100\%$-pinned fork to learn something about the factors of a semiprime $N = pq$. What survives?

Only the product's class is visible, so the observable is $S = g_1g_2$ and the fork becomes "$p$ splits or $q$ splits". Three theorems close the door.

* **Universality.** The information is a single function $D(n)$ of the group order alone — every field sits on one curve. For a cyclic cubic, $D(3) = \log 3 - \tfrac59\log5 - \tfrac29\log2 = 0.0728$ bits (measured $0.0718$).
* **Quadratic collapse with a sharp constant.** $D(n) \le \frac{1}{(2n-1)(n-1)}$, and $n^2 D(n) \to 1 - \log 2 = 0.30685$, with $n^2 D(n) < 1$ for every $n$.
* **The which-factor wall.** For any statistic of the first factor alone, the information carried by the class of $N$ is **exactly zero** — and this persists for products of any number of primes.

{{interactive_demo:1}}

{{visualization:0}}

<details>
<summary><b>Why the wall is exactly zero, not merely small</b></summary>

Fix $g_1$. The map $g_2 \mapsto g_1 g_2$ is a bijection of the group, so conditioned on $g_1$, the product is *exactly* uniform — independent of $g_1$ and of every function of it. Independence gives mutual information exactly $0$. Re-associating $p_1\cdots p_{k+1} = (p_1\cdots p_k)\,p_{k+1}$ extends this to any number of factors.
</details>

## 10. The moral

Strip away the number theory and one principle remains: **abelian observations see abelian quotients.** Any measurement channel that factors through a commutative group is blind, by construction, to everything inside the commutator subgroup. Whether a question is answerable is not a matter of effort, cleverness, or bigger computations — it is a matter of whether the question is a function on the abelianization.

A striking corollary: a quintic whose Galois group is $A_5$, a perfect group, is **completely congruence-blind**. Not one bit of its splitting behaviour is predictable from any residue class, ever.

conjectured; the proof is the sub-additivity of the binary entropy, which is in turn the
concavity of `x ↦ -x log x` anchored at `negMulLog 1 = 0`.

Main results:

* `ForkPinning.negMulLog_add_le` : `negMulLog (a+b) ≤ negMulLog a + negMulLog b`.
* `ForkPinning.negMulLog_one_sub_add` : the complementary inequality, from concavity.
* `ForkPinning.binEntropy_add_le` : **sub-additivity of the binary entropy** on `a + b ≤ 1`.
* `ForkPinning.mutualInfo_balanced_eq` : the exact two-coset decomposition of `I(X;Y)`.
* `ForkPinning.mutualInfo_le_singleCoset` : the extremal bound above.
* `ForkPinning.mutualInfo_singleCoset_eq` : single-coset forks attain it.
-/

import Probability.ForkPinningCapacity
import Probability.ForkPinningSemiprimeGeneral

namespace ForkPinning

open Finset Real

/-! ## Sub-additivity of the binary entropy -/

/-- Super-additivity of `x ↦ -x log x`, in two-term form. -/
lemma negMulLog_add_le (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) :
    negMulLog (a + b) ≤ negMulLog a + negMulLog b := by
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le ha with h | ha'
  · simp [← h]
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hb with h | hb'
  · simp [← h]
  have hs : 0 < a + b := by linarith
  have h1 : a * Real.log ((a + b) / a) ≥ 0 := by
    have h1' : 1 ≤ (a + b) / a := (one_le_div ha').mpr (by linarith)
    have := Real.log_nonneg h1'
    positivity
  have h2 : b * Real.log ((a + b) / b) ≥ 0 := by
    have h2' : 1 ≤ (a + b) / b := (one_le_div hb').mpr (by linarith)
    have := Real.log_nonneg h2'
    positivity
  have e1 : a * Real.log ((a + b) / a) = a * Real.log (a + b) - a * Real.log a := by
    rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hs) (ne_of_gt ha')]; ring
  have e2 : b * Real.log ((a + b) / b) = b * Real.log (a + b) - b * Real.log b := by
    rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hs) (ne_of_gt hb')]; ring
  simp only [negMulLog]
  nlinarith [h1, h2, e1, e2]

/-- The complementary inequality: `-x log x` evaluated on the *complements* is super-additive
as well, by concavity anchored at `negMulLog 1 = 0`. -/
lemma negMulLog_one_sub_add (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b ≤ 1) :
    negMulLog (1 - (a + b)) ≤ negMulLog (1 - a) + negMulLog (1 - b) := by
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (by linarith : (0 : ℝ) ≤ a + b) with h0 | h0
  · have ha0 : a = 0 := by linarith
    have hb0 : b = 0 := by linarith
    simp [ha0, hb0]
  have hconc := Real.strictConcaveOn_negMulLog.concaveOn
  have key : ∀ x : ℝ, 0 ≤ x → x ≤ a + b →
      (x / (a + b)) * negMulLog (1 - (a + b)) ≤ negMulLog (1 - x) := by
    intro x hx hxs
    have hw1 : 0 ≤ x / (a + b) := by positivity
    have hw2 : 0 ≤ 1 - x / (a + b) := by
      have : x / (a + b) ≤ 1 := (div_le_one h0).mpr hxs
      linarith
    have hsum : x / (a + b) + (1 - x / (a + b)) = 1 := by ring
    have h := hconc.2 (x := 1 - (a + b)) (y := 1) (by simp; linarith) (by simp) hw1 hw2 hsum
    have harg : (x / (a + b)) • (1 - (a + b)) + (1 - x / (a + b)) • (1 : ℝ) = 1 - x := by
      simp only [smul_eq_mul]
      field_simp
      ring
    rw [harg] at h
    simpa using h
  have h1 := key a ha (by linarith)
  have h2 := key b hb (by linarith)
  have hsplit : (a / (a + b)) * negMulLog (1 - (a + b)) + (b / (a + b)) * negMulLog (1 - (a + b))
      = negMulLog (1 - (a + b)) := by
    field_simp
  linarith [h1, h2, hsplit]

/-- **Sub-additivity of the binary entropy.**  Splitting a mass `a + b ≤ 1` into two parts never
decreases the total binary entropy. -/
theorem binEntropy_add_le (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b ≤ 1) :
    Real.binEntropy (a + b) ≤ Real.binEntropy a + Real.binEntropy b := by
  rw [Real.binEntropy_eq_negMulLog_add_negMulLog_one_sub,
    Real.binEntropy_eq_negMulLog_add_negMulLog_one_sub,
    Real.binEntropy_eq_negMulLog_add_negMulLog_one_sub]
  linarith [negMulLog_add_le a b ha hb, negMulLog_one_sub_add a b ha hb hab]

/-! ## The two-coset decomposition of the mutual information -/

section TwoCoset

variable {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω]

omit [Nonempty Ω] in
/-- On a fibre of positive probability the conditional law of a binary fork is `(p, 1 − p)`. -/
lemma condPrb_false_eq (X Y : Ω → Bool) (k : Bool) (hk : 0 < prb X k) :
    condPrb X Y k false = 1 - condPrb X Y k true := by
  have hsum : prb (joint X Y) (k, false) + prb (joint X Y) (k, true) = prb X k := by
    have h := sum_prb_joint X Y k
    simpa [Fintype.sum_bool, add_comm] using h
  rw [condPrb, condPrb, eq_sub_iff_add_eq, ← add_div, hsum]
  exact div_self (ne_of_gt hk)

omit [Nonempty Ω] in
/-- The fibrewise entropy of a binary fork is the binary entropy of its conditional density. -/
lemma condEntropyAt_bool (X Y : Ω → Bool) (k : Bool) (hk : 0 < prb X k) :
    condEntropyAt X Y k = Real.binEntropy (condPrb X Y k true) := by
  rw [condEntropyAt, Real.binEntropy_eq_negMulLog_add_negMulLog_one_sub]
  rw [Fintype.sum_bool, condPrb_false_eq X Y k hk]

/-- **The two-coset decomposition.**  For a balanced observable the information about a fork is
the fork's binary entropy minus the average of the two conditional binary entropies. -/
theorem mutualInfo_balanced_eq (X Y : Ω → Bool) (hX : prb X true = 1 / 2) :
    mutualInfo X Y = Real.binEntropy (prb Y true)
      - (Real.binEntropy (condPrb X Y true true)
          + Real.binEntropy (condPrb X Y false true)) / 2 := by
  have hXf : prb X false = 1 / 2 := by
    have := prb_true_add_false X
    linarith [hX]
  have hpt : (0 : ℝ) < prb X true := by rw [hX]; norm_num
  have hpf : (0 : ℝ) < prb X false := by rw [hXf]; norm_num
  have hHY : H Y = Real.binEntropy (prb Y true) := by
    rw [H_bool Y, Real.binEntropy_eq_negMulLog_add_negMulLog_one_sub]
    have hfalse : prb Y false = 1 - prb Y true := by
      have := prb_true_add_false Y
      linarith
    rw [hfalse]
    ring
  rw [mutualInfo_eq_entropy_sub_condEntropy, hHY, Fintype.sum_bool,
    condEntropyAt_bool X Y true hpt, condEntropyAt_bool X Y false hpf, hX, hXf]
  ring

/-- The two conditional densities average to the fork's density. -/
lemma condPrb_add_eq (X Y : Ω → Bool) (hX : prb X true = 1 / 2) :
    condPrb X Y true true + condPrb X Y false true = 2 * prb Y true := by
  have hXf : prb X false = 1 / 2 := by
    have := prb_true_add_false X
    linarith [hX]
  have hmarg : prb (joint X Y) (true, true) + prb (joint X Y) (false, true) = prb Y true := by
    have h := sum_prb_joint_right X Y true
    simpa [Fintype.sum_bool] using h
  rw [condPrb, condPrb, hX, hXf]
  field_simp
  linarith [hmarg]

/-- **C1, the extremal half.**  For a balanced congruence observable, a fork of density
`d ≤ 1/2` can never be pinned better than the single-coset fork of the same density. -/
theorem mutualInfo_le_singleCoset (X Y : Ω → Bool) (hX : prb X true = 1 / 2)
    (hd : prb Y true ≤ 1 / 2) :
    mutualInfo X Y
      ≤ Real.binEntropy (prb Y true) - Real.binEntropy (2 * prb Y true) / 2 := by
  have hsum := condPrb_add_eq X Y hX
  have ha : 0 ≤ condPrb X Y true true :=
    div_nonneg (prb_nonneg _ _) (prb_nonneg _ _)
  have hb : 0 ≤ condPrb X Y false true :=
    div_nonneg (prb_nonneg _ _) (prb_nonneg _ _)
  have hab : condPrb X Y true true + condPrb X Y false true ≤ 1 := by
    rw [hsum]; linarith
  have hsub := binEntropy_add_le (condPrb X Y true true) (condPrb X Y false true) ha hb hab
  rw [hsum] at hsub
  rw [mutualInfo_balanced_eq X Y hX]
  linarith [hsub]

/-- **The bound is attained.**  A fork supported inside the coset `{X = true}` realises the
extremal value: single-coset forks are exactly the best-pinned forks of their density. -/
theorem mutualInfo_singleCoset_eq (X Y : Ω → Bool) (hX : prb X true = 1 / 2)
    (hsupp : ∀ ω, Y ω = true → X ω = true) :
    mutualInfo X Y
      = Real.binEntropy (prb Y true) - Real.binEntropy (2 * prb Y true) / 2 := by
  have hzero : prb (joint X Y) (false, true) = 0 := by
    have hempty : fiber (joint X Y) (false, true) = ∅ := by
      rw [fiber, Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
      intro ω _ hcon
      have h1 : X ω = false := congrArg Prod.fst hcon
      have h2 : Y ω = true := congrArg Prod.snd hcon
      rw [hsupp ω h2] at h1
      exact Bool.noConfusion h1
    rw [prb, hempty]
    simp
  have hbzero : condPrb X Y false true = 0 := by
    rw [condPrb, hzero, zero_div]
  have hsum := condPrb_add_eq X Y hX
  rw [hbzero, add_zero] at hsum
  rw [mutualInfo_balanced_eq X Y hX, hbzero, hsum]
  simp [Real.binEntropy_zero]

end TwoCoset

  invFun q := ((q.1.1, q.2), q.1.2)

/-! ## The elementary Gibbs term of the data-processing inequality -/

/-- `r log r − r log (q p / P) ≥ r − q p / P`, in the additively split form used below. -/
lemma dpi_term {r p q P : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hrp : r ≤ p) (hrq : r ≤ q) (hqP : q ≤ P)
    (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hP : 0 ≤ P) :
    r - q * p / P
      ≤ r * Real.log r - r * Real.log q - r * Real.log p + r * Real.log P := by
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hr with h0 | h0
  · have : 0 ≤ q * p / P := by
      have hq : 0 ≤ q := le_trans hr hrq
      positivity
    rw [← h0]
    simpa using this
  · have hp0 : 0 < p := lt_of_lt_of_le h0 hrp
    have hq0 : 0 < q := lt_of_lt_of_le h0 hrq
    have hP0 : 0 < P := lt_of_lt_of_le hq0 hqP
    have hu0 : 0 < q * p / P := by positivity
    have hlog : Real.log ((q * p / P) / r) ≤ (q * p / P) / r - 1 :=
      Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (by positivity)
    have hsplit : Real.log ((q * p / P) / r)
        = Real.log q + Real.log p - Real.log P - Real.log r := by
      rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hu0) (ne_of_gt h0), Real.log_div (by positivity) (ne_of_gt hP0),

    rw [hsplit] at hlog
    have hmul := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hlog (le_of_lt h0)
    have hfield : r * ((q * p / P) / r - 1) = q * p / P - r := by field_simp
    nlinarith [hmul, hfield]

/-- The **strict** Gibbs term: strict unless the fine cell is exactly the coarse cell rescaled. -/
lemma dpi_term_lt {r p q P : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hrp : r ≤ p) (hrq : r ≤ q) (hqP : q ≤ P)

      < r * Real.log r - r * Real.log q - r * Real.log p + r * Real.log P := by
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hr with h0 | h0

    have hnn : 0 ≤ q * p / P := div_nonneg (mul_nonneg hq hp) (le_trans hq hqP)
    have hpos : 0 < q * p / P := lt_of_le_of_ne hnn (by rw [← h0] at hne; exact hne)
    rw [← h0]

  · have hp0 : 0 < p := lt_of_lt_of_le h0 hrp
    have hq0 : 0 < q := lt_of_lt_of_le h0 hrq
    have hP0 : 0 < P := lt_of_lt_of_le hq0 hqP
    have hu0 : 0 < q * p / P := by positivity

      apply hne

      linear_combination -hx

    have hsplit : Real.log ((q * p / P) / r)

    rw [hsplit] at hlog
    have hmul := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hlog h0
    have hfield : r * ((q * p / P) / r - 1) = q * p / P - r := by field_simp
    nlinarith [hmul, hfield]

lemma dpi_term_eq_zero {r p q P : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hrp : r ≤ p) (hrq : r ≤ q) (hqP : q ≤ P)

  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hr with h0 | h0
  · rw [← h0]; simp
  · have hp0 : 0 < p := lt_of_lt_of_le h0 hrp
    have hq0 : 0 < q := lt_of_lt_of_le h0 hrq
    have hP0 : 0 < P := lt_of_lt_of_le hq0 hqP
    have hlogr : Real.log r = Real.log q + Real.log p - Real.log P := by
      rw [h, Real.log_div (by positivity) (ne_of_gt hP0),
        Real.log_mul (ne_of_gt hq0) (ne_of_gt hp0)]
    rw [hlogr]; ring

/-- The pointwise information gap of the data-processing inequality: the amount by which the
cell `(k, b)` of the fine joint law fails to be the corresponding coarse cell rescaled. -/
noncomputable def dpiGap (g : κ → κ') (X : Ω → κ) (Y : Ω → β) (k : κ) (b : β) : ℝ :=
  (prb (joint X Y) (k, b) * Real.log (prb (joint X Y) (k, b))
      - prb (joint X Y) (k, b) * Real.log (prb (joint (fun ω => g (X ω)) Y) (g k, b))
      - prb (joint X Y) (k, b) * Real.log (prb X k)
      + prb (joint X Y) (k, b) * Real.log (prb (fun ω => g (X ω)) (g k)))
    - (prb (joint X Y) (k, b)
      - prb (joint (fun ω => g (X ω)) Y) (g k, b) * prb X k
          / prb (fun ω => g (X ω)) (g k))
